header.statement: Unpinned. No hardware counters. macOS has no thread pinning, and no unprivileged hardware counters. Each system gets the same thread budget.

label: A full day of tick-store alone: every record of the pinned day, every query as BENCHMARKS.md defines it with nothing clipped, and no other system. The four-system full day runs on Linux only; this gives the targets whose host is Both their figure on this host. No figure here is compared with another system's.

heap.statement: QuestDB did not run: tick-store ran alone. The full-day capacity check is Linux only.

input.ratio_baseline: The day's source bytes: every ITCH frame with its two-byte length prefix, the decompressed file, which is what BENCHMARKS.md's stored bytes must be able to rebuild.
input.clipping: A whole day. Nothing is clipped: Q2 and Q3 run over the hour [09:30:00, 10:30:00), the busiest locate is the busiest over that hour of the day, and Q5 scans every record.
input.ingest_input: tick-store ingests the day's ITCH file itself, so its write time holds ITCH parsing. The other systems ingest the columns tools/tick_export wrote from the same day, already parsed, and their times do not. Nothing is subtracted.

method.warm: Before the warm queries the day's ITCH file, its export and every store file are evicted from the page cache, each proven at 0 resident, as on Linux. Then every store file is read through by tick_coldcache warm, and mincore on a fresh mapping must read 100% of its pages resident before and after all repetitions of every query: the slice's proof, which holds on the day because tick-store's day store fits this host's memory many times over. The per-process proof of the four-system day reads /proc, which this host does not have.
method.cold: Service stopped. A fresh read-only MAP_SHARED mapping and msync(MS_INVALIDATE) per file, repeated until mincore reads 0 on every file. A fresh process then opens the store, with the server started again where there is one, and runs the query once. File system metadata stays warm. iostat's machine-wide disk0 delta must reach the bytes that became resident: a shortfall is conclusive, and an excess is not.
method.cold_includes: Each cold number is the query alone, in a fresh process. The server's start and the worker's imports fall before the clock, pyarrow.dataset and pyarrow.acero among them, and pages they touched count as resident and as device reads. The clock does hold what an engine sets up on its first call in a process: for Parquet on macOS, about 1 ms over a second call on warm pages.
method.tickstore_queries: tick-store's queries go to one tools/tick_query worker per store, started before the clock. Each is timed from Python as a round trip that stops on the worker's acknowledgement that the answer is in its memory. The worker then digests the answer by compare/queries.py's rule, outside the clock, as the other systems' digests are made in Python, and returns no rows to Python. Its engine time is recorded beside each round trip and is not the number compared. The writer and the worker each run on one thread.
method.input_cache: tick-store's write reads the day's ITCH file, 8.25 GB, which is read through first and must be resident, as on the slice. No other system ran, so no export is read inside a clock.
method.p99: nearest rank, so a small n gives a value that really occurred

swap.method: Host-wide counts of pages swapped in and out, read before and after each phase: write, read-back, warm queries and cold queries, for each variant and class. Each query's swap_timed is read just before and after its timed repetitions alone. A count says how many pages moved while the phase ran, not whose they were.
swap.timed_policy: A timed query with any page swapped in is flagged, the same way for every system: its number is kept and marked, and a verdict that rests on it says so. It is neither rerun nor refused, since a host-wide count cannot say whose page came back.

method.writes: One write per class and variant, each a sustained run of minutes over the whole day, so a write's median is that one write. Three of each would not fit the run: see compare/README.md.
method.read_back: each store read back one time window at a time, each window ordered by seq, into one column directory that tick_roundtrip verify-columns judges against the day
method.peak_memory: BSD time -l around the system's whole run, inside the measured command: the largest resident set of compare/run_system.py and every process it waited for, which counts the clean file-backed pages of every mapped file, and run_system.py's own peak memory footprint. Each worker's and tool's own peak is in its step.

parameters.name: Q1
parameters.text: One second of all symbols at the open, [09:30:00, 09:30:01).

parameters.name: Q2
parameters.text: One hour of one symbol: every record of the day's busiest locate in [09:30:00, 10:30:00).

parameters.name: Q3
parameters.text: Per-minute aggregate of one symbol over one hour: for the add orders of that locate, per minute, count, sum of shares, least and greatest price, over [09:30:00, 10:30:00).

parameters.name: Q5
parameters.text: Full scan of one column, the sum of shares, over the whole day: all 268,744,780 records.

queries.truth_method: numpy over the exported columns, sharing no code with any system

variant_selection.rule: tick-store alone, every variant it has, the headline first. The four-system full day runs on Linux only, so a host without it runs tick-store by itself, and with no other system there is nothing for the slice rule to rank.
variant_selection.source: none: no slice file chooses them

durability.reason: the writer made no flush: page_cache

write.python_note: python_seconds is the tool's start and exit, outside its own clock. engine_seconds is tick_roundtrip's own wall time: mapping the source, parsing ITCH, coding and writing the store, and its commit

detail.python_note: python_seconds is the tool's start and exit, outside its own clock. engine_seconds is tick_roundtrip's own wall time: mapping the source, parsing ITCH, coding and writing the store, and its commit
detail.input: tick-store ingests the day's ITCH file itself, so its write time holds ITCH parsing. The other systems ingest the columns tools/tick_export wrote from the same day, already parsed, and their times do not. Nothing is subtracted.
detail.clock_stops: when tick_roundtrip exits, after the rename that publishes the store and, under device_flush, its flushes

write.clock: stops when every row is readable and durable for its class

requested.input: tick-store ingests the day's ITCH file itself, so its write time holds ITCH parsing. The other systems ingest the columns tools/tick_export wrote from the same day, already parsed, and their times do not. Nothing is subtracted.
requested.hot_columns: the writer's default column specs: the eight hot dictionary columns held to ranked PFOR. Not read back: the footer names each block's codec id, not its dictionary mode
requested.codecs: each column's codec as docs/store.md lists it, zstd where the writer finds it smaller
requested.query_worker: tools/tick_query, one process per store, opened before the clock, path indexed, block CRCs checked
requested.threads: one: the writer and the query worker each run on one thread

stored.method: sum of st_blocks * 512 over every file, each inode once
stored.measured: at rest, after commit, service stopped, every file flushed first

stored_settings.g1_note: tick_roundtrip verify, the G-1 check: every record re-serialised from the store and compared with the source byte for byte, and both streams hashed. Stronger than the column oracle every system passes.

streamed.windows: none: tick_export --store reads the whole store in order
streamed.method: tick_export --store, every record through the store's read path and the ITCH encoder, straight into one column directory

inputs_evicted_before.what: the day's ITCH file and its export
inputs_evicted_before.method: msync(MS_INVALIDATE) on a fresh read-only MAP_SHARED mapping of every file

durability.sync_primitive: F_FULLFSYNC on the file, then on its directory
durability.flush_granularity: one flush per file, at its commit: the file's data before the rename that publishes it, then its directory
durability.note: F_FULLFSYNC, as LMDB and the harness's Parquet flush use
durability.reason: the writer called F_FULLFSYNC on the file, returned 0, F_FULLFSYNC on the directory, returned 0, and 0 pages stayed dirty

peak_memory.source: BSD time -l around the system's whole run, inside the measured command: the largest resident set of compare/run_system.py and every process it waited for, which counts the clean file-backed pages of every mapped file, and run_system.py's own peak memory footprint. Each worker's and tool's own peak is in its step.
